rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so I shifted weights toward stronger obfuscation while respecting that flops-5 is a tiny, hot floating-point loop benchmark (791 bytes of text, one dense main) where runtime cost dominates: SUB gets the highest benefit weights because arithmetic substitution adds real diversity to FP/ALU-heavy straight-line code at low cost, and SPLIT stays cheap and safe for structural scrambling; BCF and FLA are kept as options with high RuntimeCost weights (0.7/0.8) so the selector applies them only where control-flow features justify it, avoiding degradation of the numeric hot loops; IBR and ICALL are held at mid-levels since this binary has almost no calls or branches to disguise, making their transformation overhead hard to amortize; IGV remains enabled at modest weights for diversity despite the near-total absence of globals. Overall the table raises security/diversity pressure versus round 0 while gating the two most expensive control-flow passes behind runtime-cost sensitivity, preserving correctness (risk weights kept <=0.5) on this float-sensitive workload.
